replies.text:
Step 2 check:
- Automated abuse of a reachable endpoint: design has "customers enter a discount code" and the server "charges that amount through Stripe" — code guessing is covered (listed threat 2); however automated submission of orders/charges to Stripe itself (card testing / charge flooding) is **not covered**.
- Staff/admin/moderator screens showing user-supplied content: design mentions none — nothing to report.
- Delete/moderate/refund/role/money actions without a record of who did it: the only money action is the Stripe charge; the missing-record angle is already covered by listed threat 4 ("No server-side record of how a total was reached").
- Personal/financial documents cacheable by browsers, proxies or CDNs: design names no page or document ("sends the final price with the order to the server") — not applicable.
- Attacker text reaching logs, CSV exports, emails or headers: design states no logging, export or email — not applicable.
- Single-reviewer items: #1 and #3 duplicate listed threats 4 and 2; #4 duplicates listed threat 2; #2 (zero/negative/wrong-currency total) is the same client-supplied-amount weakness and harm as listed threat 1 — not a gap.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-07",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["browser checkout page", "discount code field", "order/checkout server endpoint", "Stripe charge call"],
    "dataStores": ["order records"],
    "externalServices": ["Stripe"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["browser to server", "server to Stripe"],
    "dataClasses": ["payment"],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Scripted checkout submissions run up Stripe charge attempts and fees",
      "scenario": "Anyone who can reach checkout scripts the order submission, which the server passes straight to Stripe as a charge. With no stated limit on submissions, an attacker fires thousands of orders with varying card details, using the endpoint as a free card-testing oracle and generating failed-payment and dispute fees. The same loop floods the merchant's Stripe account and order records, degrading real checkouts and risking Stripe rate limiting or account review.",
      "component": "Checkout order endpoint -> Stripe charge",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "availability" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The browser computes the discounted total and sends the final price with the order to the server, which charges that amount through Stripe." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V11.1.4"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-770"],
      "plainLanguage": "Nothing stops a script from firing endless checkout attempts, so an attacker can test stolen cards and pile up Stripe fees and junk orders.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Rate limit and monitor checkout charge attempts",
        "given": "an unauthenticated client submitting orders to the checkout endpoint",
        "when": "submissions from the same source, card fingerprint or session exceed a configured threshold, or the failure rate rises",
        "then": "the server rejects or challenges further attempts before calling Stripe and raises an alert, instead of forwarding every submission as a charge"
      }
    }
  ]
}
